findings.title: CVE-2026-64507: x86/bugs: Enable IBPB flush on BPF JIT allocation
findings.summary_md: The Linux kernel CVE team announced this fix on 2026-07-25, two months before the VUSec public disclosure. The kernel issues an IBPB flush when BPF JIT memory is reused, skipped when the BPF dispatcher already uses a retpoline, and guarded by CONFIG_BPF_JIT. The issue was introduced in kernel 5.18 and is fixed in 6.1.183, 6.6.145, 6.12.97, 6.18.39, 7.1.4, and mainline 7.2, touching arch/x86/kernel/cpu/bugs.c and arch/x86/include/asm/nospec-branch.h.

findings.title: CVE-2026-64508: bpf: Support for hardening against JIT spraying
findings.summary_md: Announced in the same 2026-07-25 batch, this fix flushes indirect branch predictors before BPF JIT memory is reused, via a new bpf_arch_pred_flush_enabled static key and bpf_arch_pred_flush static call. Allocations larger than a pack are not covered, which the announcement states is safe because unprivileged cBPF programs are bounded well below a pack size. Fixed in the same stable versions (6.1.183, 6.6.145, 6.12.97, 6.18.39, 7.1.4, 7.2), affecting kernel/bpf/core.c and include/linux/filter.h.

findings.title: [GR-77766] Randomize runtime code cache mappings with allocator hints
findings.summary_md: Oracle merged this change into GraalVM's master branch on 2026-08-19, randomizing runtime code cache mappings with allocator hints. VUSec's Branch Target Reuse page cites this pull request as Oracle's deployed GraalVM mitigation, which hinders JIT code-cache region reuse instead of adding predictor flushes. It landed about six weeks before the research went public.
